value.title: TopologySpec Zod contract, 30-code structural validator, and the module-graph execution boundary
value.description: Add the topology data contract and its validator as net-new modules with zero wiring into any existing execution path. Defines the discriminated node union (llm|tool|gate|router|subgraph), edges, closed router outcome labels, ports, channels, loop bounds, effect tags, cache policies, model tiers and subgraph declarations as Zod. Implements validateTopology with 30 distinct named diagnostic codes plus one malformed fixture per code, canonicalize and checksumTopology. Installs an ESLint no-restricted-imports boundary so src/pge/topology/** cannot import any executor, making zero-execution-during-validation a property of the module graph rather than of an assertion.

successCriteria.description: TopologySpecSchema parses a well-formed fixture carrying formatVersion, graphId, graphVersion, description, provenance, entry, defaults, channels, nodes, edges, subgraphs and a sha256 checksum, and rejects each field's malformed variant with a Zod issue path.

NodeSchema is a discriminated union on kind; a table-driven test enumerates every node of a fixture graph and asserts each llm node carries a promptRef, no tool node carries a promptRef, and every router node declares at least one entry in targets.

validateTopology returns ok:false with exactly the expected DiagnosticCode for each of 30 malformed fixtures under src/pge/topology/__fixtures__/, covering at minimum EmptyGraph, DuplicateNodeId, DanglingEdge, UnreachableNode, NoTerminalPath, UndeclaredPort, PortTypeMismatch, UnboundedCycle, BoundaryNotGated, NestedCheckpointer, SubgraphDepthExceeded, SubgraphExitNotSupervisor, CacheOnEffectfulNode, InterruptInsideFanOut, ModelTierMismatch, UndeclaredRouteLabel and RouterTargetNotDeclared.

validateTopology never throws for any input including non-object, null and deeply malformed JSON; a fuzz-style table asserts it always returns a ValidationReport with an ok boolean and a diagnostics array.

PortTypeMismatch names both the source and target node ids and the offending field path, asserted against a fixture whose edge connects a producer output schema to an incompatible consumer input schema.

A static walk over a fixture topology enumerates every cycle via Tarjan strongly-connected components and asserts each cycle contains a node declaring counterKey and maxIterations; a fixture adding a cyclic edge without one produces UnboundedCycle.

Structural rules covering supervisor topology hold: max subgraph nesting depth is at most 2, every subgraph exit edge targets the supervisor node, every edge crossing a subgraph boundary passes through a node of kind gate, and subgraphs[].persistence is the literal 'inherit' so a nested checkpointer is unrepresentable.

canonicalize produces a stable string with sorted keys, arrays ordered by id and the checksum field elided, and checksumTopology over that string yields a value matching the sha256:<64 hex> pattern; two structurally identical specs with different key order produce the identical checksum.

Running `npm run lint` fails when a test file placed under src/pge/topology/ imports from src/pge/runtime/, src/pge/nodes/, src/orchestrator/ or src/providers/, proving the no-restricted-imports boundary is active for that directory.
npm run typecheck, npm run typecheck:tests and npm run build all complete with zero errors.
The full Vitest suite passes with no failures versus the pre-sprint baseline of approximately 5,083 tests.

Do not register a `bober pge` CLI command or touch src/cli/index.ts; nothing in this sprint is reachable from a user-invocable entry point.
Do not add 'pge' to the pipeline.engine enum or touch src/config/schema.ts.
Do not implement render, diff, docs-drift, state-audit or optimize — sprint 3 owns the toolkit.
Do not create src/pge/runtime/, src/pge/nodes/ or src/pge/registry/ even as empty placeholders.
Do not modify src/orchestrator/pipeline.ts, src/orchestrator/workflow/** or any provider adapter.
stopConditions: All 30 diagnostic codes have a dedicated malformed fixture and an assertion pinning that exact code.
The ESLint boundary is proven by a deliberately violating fixture that makes `npm run lint` exit non-zero.
A required criterion cannot be met without wiring the new modules into an existing execution path.
A rule would require importing an executor into src/pge/topology/, which the boundary forbids by design.

value.generatorNotes: Copy the ESLint boundary idiom verbatim from eslint.config.js:46-48 (telemetry local-only) and :75-77 (medical zero-egress) — a files-scoped block with no-restricted-imports patterns. Reuse the existing __fixtures__ directory convention already used by src/orchestrator/__fixtures__ and src/orchestrator/workflow/__fixtures__. Confirm no file under src/pge/topology/ transitively reaches an executor by inspecting the import graph, not by trusting the lint rule alone. Confirm validateTopology has no side effects at all — no fs writes, no process spawn, no network. Check that the 30 fixtures are genuinely 30 distinct codes and not duplicates with different names. Confirm src/contracts/index.ts gained only an export line.

value.title: Authored CODING_GRAPH literal, `bober pge` CLI, and the committed checksummed topology artifact
value.description: Author the shipped coding pipeline as a plain typed object literal (export const CODING_GRAPH: TopologySpec) covering every node in the architecture blueprint — research subgraph, planner with clarification loop, supervisor, sprint subgraph, gates, routers, evaluation, synthesis, documenter, gated commit, graceful failure and context compaction. Add the `bober pge` CLI with dump, validate and hash verbs, and commit the serialized artifact to .bober/topology/coding.json so it becomes the load-bearing contract the runtime will later read. Proves topology/content separation: a prompt edit leaves the checksum untouched, an edge addition changes it, and swapping model profiles produces an identical hash.

successCriteria.description: src/pge/topology/coding.graph.ts exports CODING_GRAPH typed as TopologySpec, it parses through TopologySpecSchema, and validateTopology in structural mode returns ok:true with zero error-severity diagnostics.

The authored graph contains every node named in the architecture mermaid blueprint, asserted by a pinned node-id list covering the research, plan, sprint, evaluation, terminal and context-compaction regions, so a silently dropped node fails the test.

`bober pge dump` writes .bober/topology/coding.json containing graphId, graphVersion matching the semver pattern, provenance 'authored', every node id, every node kind and every edge, and the file parses back through TopologySpecSchema.
`bober pge dump --check` exits 0 when the committed artifact matches the canonicalised literal byte for byte and exits non-zero after a single-character mutation of the committed file.
`bober pge validate` exits non-zero and prints the diagnostic code name for each of the 30 malformed fixtures from sprint 1, and exits 0 for the committed artifact.
A test substitutes a spy for every node executor lookup and asserts zero invocations across dump, validate and hash, complementing the sprint-1 lint boundary with a behavioural assertion.
Mutating a prompt body under the prompt store and recomputing `bober pge hash` leaves the topology checksum unchanged, while adding one edge to the literal changes it.

Running dump under two different model configurations produces identical topology checksums while the resolved model ids recorded for the run differ, proving a model-profile swap is not a structural change.

checksumTopology recomputed from the committed artifact's canonicalised node and edge list equals the checksum field stored in that artifact, and a stale checksum surfaces as the ChecksumStale diagnostic rather than silently passing.
npm run typecheck, npm run typecheck:tests, npm run build and npm run lint complete with zero errors and the full Vitest suite is green.

nonGoals: Do not implement any node body, node registry or executor — this sprint produces data and a reader, nothing runnable.
Do not add render, diff, docs or audit-state verbs to the CLI; sprint 3 owns them and adding stubs now creates dead command surface.
Do not call EffectRegistry.seal() from dump in this sprint — the registry does not exist yet, and importing it would violate the sprint-1 boundary. Sprint 5 adds the seal call.
Do not add .bober/topology/ to .gitignore — this directory is deliberately version-controlled.
Do not change pipeline.engine, the engine seam, or any orchestrator file.
stopConditions: The committed artifact round-trips: literal to canonical form to file to parse to identical checksum.
`bober pge dump --check` fails on a mutated artifact and passes on an untouched one.
A node in the architecture blueprint cannot be expressed under the sprint-1 schema without widening Goto to accept an arbitrary node id, which ADR-3 forbids.
Authoring the literal would require importing a runtime module.
value.definitionOfDone: The coding pipeline exists as a typed literal, is serialized to a committed and checksummed .bober/topology/coding.json, and `bober pge dump|validate|hash` operate on it without any executor in the module graph. The repository is shippable: typecheck, typecheck:tests, build and lint clean, full Vitest suite green, and the only user-visible change is a new `pge` subcommand that reads and writes topology data.

A thin `bober graph topology <verb>` alias may be added later; both rename cleanly now and expensively after the CI job exists.

Documenting the nodes in docs/pge-graph.md — sprint 14.

value.title: Topology toolkit — mermaid/dot render, structural diff with route labels, doc-drift check, state audit, optimisation hook
value.description: Complete Layer A by deriving every inspection artifact from the committed topology alone. Adds renderTopology for mermaid and dot, diffTopology reporting node, edge, channel and router-outcome-label additions, removals, renames and field changes, checkDocDrift comparing documented node ids to artifact node ids, generateStateAudit deriving every state key's writers and readers from nodes[].writes/reads, and optimizeTopology which applies a caller-supplied mutation, re-validates the result and records a per-variant score. Surfaces all five through the `bober pge` CLI. This is the sprint that makes the graph a versionable, diffable, optimisable engineering artifact.

successCriteria.description: `bober pge render --format mermaid` emits text that a mermaid parser accepts without error, pinned by a snapshot of the committed coding topology; adding one node to a fixture graph changes the snapshot.

renderTopology with format 'dot' emits a digraph whose node count equals spec.nodes.length and whose edge count equals spec.edges.length, so the diagram is derived from the artifact rather than hand-drawn.

`bober pge diff a.json b.json` emits structured JSON; a fixture pair differing by one added node and one added edge yields exactly one entry in nodesAdded, exactly one in edgesAdded and empty nodesRemoved and edgesRemoved.
Diffing a file against itself produces empty:true and exit code 0, and diffing two files that differ only in key ordering also produces empty:true because both are canonicalised first.

Adding one outcome label to a router's targets produces exactly one routeLabelsAdded entry naming the router and the label, so a change to routing behaviour can never present as an empty structural diff.
diffTopology reports graphVersion.from, graphVersion.to and a bumped boolean, and a fixture pair with structural changes and an unchanged graphVersion sets bumped:false.
checkDocDrift returns the symmetric difference between node ids in a markdown doc and node ids in the artifact, returning an empty array only when the two sets are equal.

`bober pge audit-state` writes .bober/topology/state-audit.json in which every channel key has at least one declared writer, no writer id exists outside spec.nodes, and running the command twice produces byte-identical output.

optimizeTopology applied to a mutator that swaps one node's promptRef and drops one optional gate returns a spec that passes validateTopology, sets provenance to 'optimizer', writes a per-variant score record under .bober/topology/variants/, and performs zero node executions.
npm run typecheck, npm run typecheck:tests, npm run build and npm run lint complete with zero errors and the full Vitest suite is green.

nonGoals: Do not add any CI workflow job — sprint 14 owns the blocking gate; wiring it now would gate merges on tooling that has no golden dataset behind it.
Do not author docs/pge-graph.md; this sprint delivers the drift checker, sprint 14 delivers the document it checks.
Do not implement an automated search strategy, scoring model or variant-promotion command for the optimiser — the mutation and re-validation hook only.
Do not let the optimiser's variant output participate in `dump --check`, which applies only to provenance 'authored'.
Do not import any runtime, node or orchestrator module; the sprint-1 boundary still governs this directory.
stopConditions: All five derivations run against the committed .bober/topology/coding.json and produce deterministic output.
The route-label diff case is proven with a fixture whose only change is inside a router's targets array.
A derivation would require executing a node or resolving a live prompt body to produce its output.
value.definitionOfDone: renderTopology, diffTopology, checkDocDrift, generateStateAudit and optimizeTopology exist with paired tests, all five are reachable through `bober pge`, and every one derives its result from the artifact with no executor in the module graph. The repository is shippable: typecheck, typecheck:tests, build and lint clean, full Vitest suite green, and no existing execution path changed.
assumptions: The state audit derives writers and readers from nodes[].writes/reads because ADR-4 forbids storing them a second time on channels[], so there is exactly one encoding to read.
The per-variant score record is a placeholder schema whose score field may be null until a golden dataset exists in sprint 14; the hook exists so an optimiser can be written offline.
diffTopology throws TypeError when either input fails TopologySpecSchema.parse rather than returning a partial diff.
outOfScope: Rendering runtime traces or executed paths — this renders topology, not history.
Any diff of prompt bodies; prompt content is deliberately outside the topology.
value.generatorNotes: Keep each derivation in its own small module under src/pge/topology/ per the repo's small-utility-module principle: render.ts, diff.ts, docs.ts, audit.ts, optimize.ts. Canonicalise both inputs before diffing so key ordering never produces a spurious diff. Node renames are detected by matching an added and a removed node whose full field set is identical apart from id; anything else is reported as add plus remove rather than a guessed rename. For mermaid, node shapes should follow the architecture blueprint's convention (subgraph as {{...}}, hitl as [[...]], terminals as (...)), because the snapshot in sprint 14's documentation is compared against this output. state-audit.json must include generatedFrom { graphId, checksum } so a stale audit is detectable.
value.evaluatorNotes: Confirm the diff is genuinely structural and not textual — reorder the nodes array in one input and assert the diff is still empty. Confirm route-label detection is not conflated with edge detection: a label added to an existing router with no new edge must still be reported. Confirm audit-state determinism by running it twice in one test and comparing bytes, not by comparing parsed objects. Confirm optimizeTopology returns a NEW spec and does not mutate its input. Confirm the variants directory is written under .bober/topology/variants/ and is excluded from dump --check.

value.title: Engine-seam hardening, single terminal side-effect owner, and enforced loop bounds on the live imperative path
value.description: Prepare the shipped path before any graph code depends on it. Exports PIPELINE_ENGINE_NAMES as the single source for both Zod engine enums and adds 'pge' as a fifth name with no implementation behind it. Replaces the ad-hoc opts object with a named RunOptions and widens the pipelineFn signatures in mcp/run-manager.ts and orchestrator/worktree.ts that currently pass fields the interface does not declare. Extracts finalizePipelineRun from pipeline.ts so the pipeline-complete history event and the <runId>.completed.json marker have exactly one emitter shared by TsPipelineEngine and RunResultFlusher, repairing the pre-existing divergence where the flusher writes neither. Finally retrofits enforced retry counters and maximum-iteration bounds onto the currently live cyclic paths so runaway budget burn is bounded today rather than after the port.

successCriteria.description: PIPELINE_ENGINE_NAMES is exported once from src/orchestrator/workflow/engine.ts as a const tuple including 'pge', PipelineEngineName is derived from it, and both the pipeline.engine enum at config/schema.ts and the teams[].pipelineShape enum are constructed from that same tuple rather than repeating string literals.

A test asserts config.pipeline.engine still defaults to 'ts', that 'pge' parses as a valid enum value, and that resolveEngineName downgrades 'pge' to 'ts' with a logged line while no PgeEngine implementation exists.

PipelineEngine.run declares a named RunOptions type covering runId, teamId, now, signal and resume, and the pipelineFn parameter types in mcp/run-manager.ts and orchestrator/worktree.ts accept it, so passing teamId or now no longer relies on structural widening that the interface does not declare.

finalizePipelineRun is exported from src/orchestrator/finalize.ts, PIPELINE_COMPLETE_EVENT and COMPLETION_MARKER_SUFFIX are exported constants, and src/chat/completion-tailer.ts imports the marker suffix constant instead of matching an inline string literal.

An end-to-end test drives a run through TsPipelineEngine and asserts CompletionTailer.poll() yields the runId, and a second test drives RunResultFlusher.flush and asserts it emits the identical history event and completion marker that the TS engine emits.

The PipelineResult object returned by finalizePipelineRun has the same field set as the one previously built inline in pipeline.ts, asserted by a key-set snapshot so the frozen shape cannot drift during extraction.

The sprint retry path in runSprintCycle and the pure-sprint iteration loop both read a configured maximum and emit a bounded-exit event when reached; a test injecting an always-failing evaluator terminates within max+1 iterations and the test's own hard ceiling is never reached.

.gitignore gains no runtime directories in this sprint, and a test asserts the .bober/ paths that sprints 6 and 8 will create are still absent, so the ignore additions land alongside the code that creates them.

The full Vitest suite passes with no failures versus the pre-sprint baseline, specifically including src/orchestrator/pipeline.test.ts, pipeline.pause.test.ts, pipeline-run-id.test.ts, workflow/selector.test.ts, workflow/flusher.test.ts and chat completion-tailer tests.
npm run typecheck, npm run typecheck:tests, npm run build and npm run lint complete with zero errors.

Do not flip src/orchestrator/workflow/eligibility.ts away from returning false or make WorkflowEngine.invoke stop throwing; the dormant workflow path stays dormant.
Do not change the runPipeline signature at pipeline.ts:1074 or add, remove or rename any PipelineResult field.

A grep for the raw string 'pipeline-complete' and for '.completed.json' finds only the two exported constants and their imports.

value.title: Three-scope state split, closed join-semilattice reducer registry, node/effect registries and the topology compiler
value.description: Define OverallState as a small snapshot-pinned set of public Zod keys bound to the existing PlanSpec and SprintContract contracts with a compile-time drift guard, declare per-node input and output port schemas resolved through a SchemaCatalog, and confine node-local data to a NodeContext.priv map that is never a channel. Implement the closed six-reducer registry whose signature is merge(current, updates[]) called once per channel per superstep, with all four join-semilattice flags as literal true so a non-conforming reducer is unregisterable at the type level. Add NodeRegistry, EffectRegistry with a seal() that closes the effect channel during topology production, and the compiler that turns a validated artifact plus registries into a CompiledGraph with proven port assignability, failing on both unregistered node implementations and orphan implementations.

successCriteria.description: A snapshot test pins the exact OverallState key set as a sorted list; adding or removing any key fails the test until the whitelist and the pinned key-count budget are amended in the same change.

A compile-time Exact guard asserts OverallState['sprintContracts'] element type is exactly z.infer<typeof SprintContractSchema> and OverallState['spec'] is PlanSpec or null, so a parallel contract type fails npm run typecheck rather than failing at runtime.

Each of the six reducers appendById, maxNumber, lastWriteWinsByKey, setUnion, replaceIfNewer and mergeLedger passes a property test over at least 200 randomized input pairs asserting merge(merge(s,xs),ys) equals merge(s,[...xs,...ys]) exactly.
The same property suite asserts shuffle invariance of the canonicalised merged result and idempotence, so merge(s,xs) equals merge(merge(s,xs),xs) for every reducer.

A property test applies 100 randomized concurrent merges to the messages channel and asserts the list length is monotonically non-decreasing and every previously present message id survives every merge.

Attempting to register a reducer object whose associative, batchingInvariant, orderInvariant or idempotent flag is not the literal true fails npm run typecheck, proven by a type-level negative fixture.

compile() throws TopologyCompileError with an UnregisteredNodeImpl diagnostic when the artifact names a node with no registered implementation, and an OrphanNodeImpl diagnostic when a registered implementation is absent from the artifact.

compilerFidelity compiles a fixture artifact with fixture registries and asserts CompiledGraph.nodes keys equal spec.nodes ids and CompiledGraph.adjacency equals spec.edges, with the spec authoritative in both directions.

compile() asserts each registered NodeImpl's declared inputSchema and outputSchema match the schemaRef declared on that node's ports, and a mismatch produces a diagnostic naming the node id and the port key.

EffectRegistry.invoke throws EffectNotDeclaredError when an effect's tags exceed the calling node's declared effects array, and throws EffectChannelClosed after seal(); `bober pge dump` calls seal() and a test asserts an effect invocation during dump throws rather than performing the effect.
npm run typecheck, npm run typecheck:tests, npm run build and npm run lint complete with zero errors and the full Vitest suite is green.

nonGoals: Do not implement the interpreter, the frontier planner, the commit boundary or any checkpointer — this sprint produces the type substrate they consume.
Do not implement any production node body; register only fixture implementations for the compiler tests.

Do not compile the real .bober/topology/coding.json in this sprint — most of its node implementations do not exist yet and compile() correctly throws UnregisteredNodeImpl. The first full-graph compile is sprint 13.
Do not add a seventh reducer or an escape hatch that accepts an arbitrary merge function; the registry is deliberately closed.
Do not put raw tool stdout, workspace diffs or bulk payloads into any OverallState key.
Do not modify src/contracts/sprint-contract.ts or src/contracts/spec.ts — OverallState binds to them, it does not redefine them.
stopConditions: All six reducers pass associativity, batching invariance, shuffle invariance and idempotence at 200 or more randomized pairs.
compile() fails in both directions — unregistered artifact node and orphan implementation.
The 14-key snapshot is pinned and the Exact drift guard fails typecheck when deliberately broken.
A required channel needs a merge that is genuinely order-dependent, in which case the channel must be modelled as an offloaded artifact referenced by refs rather than adding a non-conforming reducer.
value.definitionOfDone: src/pge/state/overall.ts, src/pge/registry/{nodes,reducers,effects}.ts and src/pge/compile/compiler.ts exist with paired tests, OverallState is a snapshot-pinned key whitelist bound to the existing contracts by a typecheck-enforced guard, the six reducers are proven join-semilattices by property tests, and the compiler resolves every string reference or fails loudly. The repository is shippable: typecheck, typecheck:tests, build and lint clean, full Vitest suite green, and nothing outside src/pge/ changed except the seal() call added to the dump path.
assumptions: OPEN — the architecture text says 'Exactly 14 keys' but its OverallStateSchema enumerates 15: runId, projectRoot, featureRequest, specId, currentPhase, spec, sprintContracts, evaluations, messages, refs, counters, branchStatus, testAnchors, verdict, ledger. This sprint pins the enumerated set (15) and records the count in the snapshot; a human must confirm whether a key was intended to be dropped before the snapshot is treated as the whitelist.
PrivateState is a fresh Map per task on NodeContext.priv, never registered as a channel, and therefore structurally incapable of reaching the commit boundary.

value.title: Runtime substrate — content-addressed scratch, sealed archives, semantic cache, span trace, budget ledger, sandbox runner
value.description: Implement the six leaf services the interpreter will inject into every NodeContext, all as plain files under .bober/ with no database and no daemon. ScratchStore content-addresses bulk payloads so a 5 MB diff never reaches state. ArchiveWriter writes a per-node-run directory with snapshot, stdout and outputs and seals it so nothing downstream can rewrite it. SemanticCache is keyed on the exact six mandated components with a per-entry expiry driven by an injectable clock. TraceWriter appends one span per node execution to a JSONL file that is the source of truth for debugging. BudgetLedger accumulates replay-idempotent per-node cost with an enforceable ceiling. SandboxRunner executes generated code and generated tests under a command allowlist, cwd confinement and a wall-clock bound — entirely net-new, since no allowlist exists in the shipped tool layer today.

successCriteria.description: ScratchStore.put writes .bober/scratch/<runId>/<sha256>.<ext> and returns a ScratchRef carrying uri, sha256, bytes and kind; a 5 MB payload round-trips through put and get byte-identically and putting identical content twice yields one file.

A test writes a 5 MB diff through the offload path and asserts the serialized state carrying only its ScratchRef stays under 4 KB, and that a second consumer reading the referenced path receives byte-identical content.

ArchiveWriter.open creates .bober/archive/<runId>/<nodeId>[.<branchKey>]/ containing snapshot.json, stdout.log and outputs.json, and after seal() every one of writeSnapshot, appendStdout and writeOutputs rejects with ArchiveImmutableError naming the directory.

seal() writes a .sealed sidecar under the default marker mode and sets file mode 0o444 only under the opt-in chmod mode; prune restores writable mode before unlink under both settings so worktree cleanup and git clean still succeed.

SemanticCache.key hashes exactly systemPrompt, userPrompt, contextFilesHash, model, temperature and toolsMask; an identical call yields one provider invocation and one hit, and six further assertions each vary exactly one component and assert a miss.

With an injected fake clock, a cache entry hits inside its ttlSeconds and misses after expiry, prune removes expired entries and returns the count removed, and a call made with no declared policy never writes a cache file at all.

TraceWriter appends one JSONL span per node execution to .bober/traces/<runId>.jsonl carrying nodeId, parentSpanId, superstep, startedAt, endedAt, inputHash, outputHash, tokens, costUsd, cache status, toolOutputRef, route, status and errorClass; a test reconstructs the spans into a tree and asserts the tree is well formed with exactly one root.

BudgetLedger.charge keyed by nodeId, attempt and callIndex REPLACES rather than adds, so charging the same key twice leaves per-node sums equal to run totals for calls, tokens and USD; assertWithinCeiling throws a typed BudgetExceededError when a configured ceiling is passed.

SandboxRunner returns status 'denied' naming the binary when a command outside the allowlist is invoked, status 'timeout' when a non-terminating command exceeds timeoutMs rather than hanging the test, and status 'output-truncated' beyond maxOutputBytes; all three are recorded as spans and none of them throws.

value.title: Superstep interpreter, dependency- and file-conflict-aware admission, unified Command routing, single commit boundary
value.description: Deliver executable graph semantics (G3). GraphInterpreter runs a compiled graph as a Pregel loop: plan frontier, admit, execute under the shipped Scheduler and Semaphore, barrier, commit once, route. Nodes return a single Command combining a state delta and a destination — a declared route label, a node, a runtime fan-out, or the parent scope — replacing exhaustive static conditional-edge maps. FrontierPlanner becomes the first consumer of SprintContract.dependsOn anywhere in the repo and additionally serializes contracts whose declared file sets intersect, recording the reason in the trace. CommitBoundary is the sole writer of .bober/ domain artifacts and the sole clock source, applying each channel reducer exactly once per superstep with the whole batch and rejecting any channel value above its inline byte limit so bulk offloading is enforced rather than advised. Ships with the determinism and exactly-once invariant suites.

successCriteria.description: One integration test compiles a golden fixture topology, runs it against stub providers, and asserts from a single recorded trace the scheduled node order, at least one dynamic route taken, at least one loop re-entry and at least one shared-state merge.

Node returns validate against a Command Zod type with optional update and required goto; a test asserts a node returning both produces exactly one state commit and one routing decision in the trace, and a structural assertion confirms no static conditional-edge map exists for that node.
A nested node returning goto with scope 'parent' resumes control at the parent supervisor, while the same goto without the parent scope fails with UnknownNodeInScope.

A planner emitting 5 contracts produces 5 branch dispatches from a single routing decision, and re-running the same graph with 3 contracts leaves the topology checksum unchanged, proving fan-out cardinality is runtime-determined rather than encoded as a static edge per contract.

With B.dependsOn set to A, B is never dispatched before A completes; with two contracts sharing an entry in estimatedFiles, the two never run concurrently and the trace records status 'serialized' with serializedReason 'fileConflict' and both contract ids.

With deliberately staggered branch completion, the evaluator stage's first invocation timestamp is after the last branch completion and it observes exactly N results, proving the fan-in barrier holds.

A write-counter spy on CommitBoundary across 8 concurrent branches asserts writesPerChannel is exactly 1 for every touched channel per superstep, and the final artifacts are byte-identical to a sequential run of the same inputs.
The determinism suite runs the same golden fixture at concurrency 1 and concurrency 8 and asserts the resulting .bober/ artifact trees are byte-identical after canonicalisation.

Committing a channel value that serialises above the channel's maxInlineBytes is rejected with StateBloatError naming the channel and the byte count, and a node feeding a 5 MB diff must offload and pass a ScratchRef for the commit to succeed.
After a node returns, none of that node's private keys appear in merged state, while the trace shows those keys existed during that node's execution.
The trace's currentPhase sequence for the golden run equals a pinned expected sequence and no routing decision leaves the phase unset.
A fully blocked frontier returns an empty admit list and the interpreter treats it as deadlock and routes to the graceful-failure terminal rather than spinning or hanging.
npm run typecheck, npm run typecheck:tests, npm run build and npm run lint complete with zero errors and the full Vitest suite is green.

nonGoals: Do not implement checkpoint persistence, resume or HITL interrupts — sprint 8 owns durability; this sprint's interpreter runs to completion or fails in one process.
Do not implement retry policy, per-branch backoff, branch-result caching or the graceful-failure node body — sprint 9 owns resilience; this sprint only routes to the terminal on deadlock.
Do not implement any production node body; the invariant suites use fixture nodes with deterministic stub providers.
Do not raise the default fan-out concurrency above 1. Higher concurrency is opt-in per spec and always subordinate to dependsOn and file-conflict serialization.
Do not write any acceptance test that asserts a wall-clock speedup or compares elapsed time between concurrency settings.
Do not modify src/orchestrator/pipeline.ts or select the PGE engine anywhere; nothing in this sprint is reachable from a shipped run.
Do not add a second write site for .bober/ domain artifacts; CommitBoundary is the only writer and the only new Date() source.
stopConditions: The determinism suite is green at concurrency 1 and 8 with byte-identical artifacts.
The exactly-once write-counter spy reports one write per channel per superstep across 8 branches.
dependsOn and file-set intersection both demonstrably gate admission with the reason recorded in the trace.
An invariant cannot hold without making a reducer order-dependent, in which case the channel must be modelled as an offloaded artifact instead.
value.definitionOfDone: src/pge/runtime/{interpreter,frontier,commit}.ts execute a compiled graph as a superstep loop with unified Command routing, admission that honours dependsOn and serializes file conflicts, and a single commit boundary that applies each reducer once per superstep and enforces the inline byte limit. Two of the three blocking invariant suites — determinism and exactly-once — are green. The repository is shippable: typecheck, typecheck:tests, build and lint clean, full Vitest suite green, and no shipped execution path reaches the interpreter.
assumptions: Scheduler gains exactly one new method, settle, of roughly 25 lines, so a rejecting branch does not reject the whole batch the way Scheduler.parallel's Promise.all does at scheduler.ts:140. This is the only edit to a shipped runtime file in this sprint.
taskKey is sha256 of nodeId plus branchKey plus inputHash; sprint 8 uses it for resume, this sprint uses it for identity and for the file-conflict ledger.
The evaluator barrier is implicit in the superstep model: the evaluator stage is simply the next superstep after the last branch commits.

File sets come from SprintContract.estimatedFiles, which is the only declared file information available; contracts with an empty estimatedFiles are treated as conflicting with everything at concurrency above 1.
outOfScope: Context compression at superstep boundaries — sprint 10 hooks into the boundary this sprint creates.
Any conformance comparison against the TS engine — sprint 13.
value.generatorNotes: Reuse rather than reimplement: Scheduler and Semaphore (workflow/scheduler.ts:54-165) for bounded execution, Budget (budget.ts:40) for the ceiling, and the flusher's single-commit-boundary and single-clock discipline (flusher.ts:23-104) generalised from one-shot to per-superstep. The interpreter loop order is fixed: plan frontier, admit, execute, barrier, commit once, checkpoint (sprint 8), route. Reducers are invoked once per channel per superstep with the whole batch — never folded update by update, because pairwise folding is order-dependent and breaks the concurrency-1-versus-8 criterion. Goto has kinds label, node, fanout and parent; the label kind resolves through the compiled adjacency, and a label outside the router's declared targets is UndeclaredRouteLabel. The empty-admit deadlock path must be distinguishable in the trace from a normal completion. Keep the interpreter free of any direct fs write — every artifact write goes through CommitBoundary.
value.evaluatorNotes: This sprint carries the highest silent-corruption risk in the plan; weight the invariant suites above feature completeness. Verify the determinism suite compares canonicalised bytes of the artifact tree, not parsed objects, and that it genuinely runs at two different concurrency settings rather than reading a cached result. Verify the write-counter spy counts reducer invocations at the commit boundary and not node returns. Verify the file-conflict test uses two contracts with a genuine intersection and asserts the trace reason, not merely that they did not overlap by luck. Verify no test anywhere in the diff asserts elapsed time. Verify CommitBoundary is the only new Date() call site in src/pge/runtime/ by inspection.

value.title: Filesystem checkpointer, cross-process resume, superstep-boundary HITL interrupts and fail-closed gating of git and deploy
value.description: Make a run survivable and pausable. FsCheckpointer writes .bober/checkpoints/<runId>/<superstep>.json temp-file-plus-rename so a partial checkpoint is never readable, carrying state, pending tasks, completed task keys, an optional interrupt record and the graph identity so a resume against a changed topology fails loudly rather than replaying task keys into a different graph. InterruptController evaluates interrupts BEFORE a node executes, at a superstep boundary, so no node body ever re-runs on resume and the double-execution class simply does not exist. It delegates to the shipped checkpoint mechanism registry and audit writer rather than inventing a second approval path, so bober approve and bober reject keep working. Git commits and deploy actions are reachable only through a HITL gate and block fail-closed with an audit entry when no approval record exists. Ships the third blocking invariant suite (cross-process durability) plus an adversarial checkpointer conformance suite with kill-mid-write fault injection.

successCriteria.description: A run is terminated after node 3 and restarted from the persisted checkpoint in a FRESH process; executor spies for nodes 1 to 3 record zero new invocations and the final artifact equals the uninterrupted run's artifact.

An adversarial checkpointer suite exercises put, get, latest, list and prune including kill-mid-write fault injection, and asserts no partially written checkpoint is ever readable and that list never yields a ref whose get fails.

A checkpoint carries graphId, graphVersion and checksum, and resume against an artifact whose checksum differs throws ChecksumMismatch rather than replaying completed task keys against a changed graph.
Resume skips dispatch of every taskKey present in completedTaskKeys before dispatch rather than after, asserted by a spy that records dispatch attempts and not merely executions.

Triggering an interrupt returns a result with status 'interrupted', the persisted checkpoint contains the pending payload, no further node executed, and resuming continues from exactly that node with the supplied human decision present in state.

A test asserts the interrupt is evaluated before the node handler is entered — the handler spy records zero invocations for the interrupted node before resume and exactly one after — proving no node body re-runs.

A commit node and a deploy node in non-interactive mode with no recorded approval are both blocked fail-closed and written to the audit log; with an approval record present both proceed, and the audit entry names the checkpoint id in both cases.

InterruptController resolves its mechanism through the shipped getCheckpointMechanismFor registry and records outcomes through runWithAudit, asserted by a test that configures the disk mechanism and observes the audit file the existing subsystem writes.

A positive nesting test asserts a nested child subgraph resolves the parent's checkpointer handle identity, and a hand-edited artifact declaring its own persistence handle is rejected by validation with NestedCheckpointer.
With durability set to 'superstep' a checkpoint file exists per superstep and with 'exit' only at phase boundaries; both settings produce the same final artifact for the same golden fixture.
.gitignore gains .bober/checkpoints/ in the same change that creates it, and prune(runId, keep) retains exactly the requested number of most recent checkpoints.
npm run typecheck, npm run typecheck:tests, npm run build and npm run lint complete with zero errors and the full Vitest suite is green.

nonGoals: Do not implement an in-process or in-memory checkpointer, not even as a test double alternative that could be selected in production; the cross-process criterion is the discriminator and an in-memory store cannot satisfy it.
Do not use better-sqlite3 or any database for checkpoints; a checkpoint must remain readable with cat and diffable with git diff, which is the debugging affordance the whole design rests on.
Do not allow an interrupt inside a fan-out branch; InterruptInsideFanOut must reject it at validation time, and per-branch approvals batch at the fan-in barrier so one interrupt covers N branches.

Do not create a second approval path, a second audit file or a second set of checkpoint ids; delegate to the shipped subsystem so bober approve, bober reject and the nine documented checkpoint ids keep working unchanged.
Do not implement retry, backoff or partial-failure recovery — sprint 9.
Do not implement the planner clarification loop node itself; sprint 11 builds the node on top of this interrupt mechanism.
stopConditions: The fresh-process kill-and-resume test is green with zero re-invocations of completed nodes.
The adversarial checkpointer suite including kill-mid-write is green.
Every HITL path resolves through the existing mechanism registry and audit writer.
A criterion would require resuming inside a node body rather than at a superstep boundary.
value.definitionOfDone: A run can be killed and resumed in a separate CLI process without re-executing a completed node, an interrupt freezes a single consistent snapshot and resumes with the human decision in state, and git and deploy actions are unreachable without an approval record. The third blocking invariant suite is green alongside an adversarial checkpointer conformance suite. The repository is shippable: typecheck, typecheck:tests, build and lint clean, full Vitest suite green, and no shipped execution path reaches the checkpointer.
assumptions: The HITL round trip spans separate CLI invocations, which is why src/orchestrator/checkpoints/mechanisms/disk.ts already exists; the graph checkpointer complements it rather than replacing it.

durability defaults to 'superstep' for crash-safety parity with the per-contract flush discipline at flusher.ts:46-76, on the assumption that one JSON write per node is negligible against LLM latency. If measurement disagrees, 'exit' is the fallback at the cost of coarser resume.

Modelling every pause point as its own node inflates node count and forces some node-local values into refs; where an approval depends on a large intermediate result, that result is offloaded to ScratchStore rather than inlined, or the inline byte guard rejects the commit.
outOfScope: Resuming a run whose topology artifact changed — that is a deliberate ChecksumMismatch failure, not a supported migration.
Multi-run concurrent HITL; the existing one-careful-run-at-a-time limitation is unchanged.
value.generatorNotes: createFsCheckpointer takes projectRoot as a required argument and there is no module-level instance, so worktree runs stay isolated. put() writes to a temp name in the same directory then renames, which is atomic on the same filesystem — do not write in place and do not write to the OS temp directory. CompiledGraph deliberately has no checkpointer field, so a nested checkpointer is unrepresentable in the compiled form; NestedCheckpointer exists only to catch hand-edited JSON. Generalise the skip-before-dispatch discipline at workflow/resume-cursor.ts:12 from sprint numbers to task keys rather than writing a new mechanism. InterruptController.maybeInterrupt is called by the interpreter BEFORE Scheduler.settle dispatches, and raiseSuspend throws GraphInterrupted which the interpreter converts into the interrupted result — the node handler must never see it. Model the adversarial suite on the published @langchain/langgraph-checkpoint-validation contract semantics for put, get, list and delete, without taking that package as a dependency.
value.evaluatorNotes: Verify the kill-and-resume test genuinely uses a separate process (child process or spawned CLI) rather than a same-process simulation; a same-process test cannot distinguish this design from MemorySaver and would make the whole criterion vacuous. Verify the kill-mid-write injection truncates a real file rather than mocking the filesystem. Verify the interrupt-before-execution assertion inspects handler invocation counts rather than trace ordering alone. Verify the fail-closed test asserts the git operation did NOT happen, not merely that an error was returned. Verify no new checkpoint mechanism, audit path or approval CLI verb was introduced. Confirm .bober/checkpoints/ is in .gitignore in this diff.

value.title: Partial-failure resilience — branch result caching, failed-branch-only jittered retry, enforced loop counters, graceful failure terminal and qualified synthesis
value.description: Make one failing branch a bounded local event rather than a run-ending exception. Successful branch results are cached and preserved so a re-run reuses them without re-invoking their executors; only the failed branch is retried, spaced by the decorrelated jittered exponential policy the repo already ships. Every cyclic edge's loop counter is enforced at runtime against the maxIterations declared in the topology, using the idempotent counter reducer so a replayed superstep cannot double-count. When retries are exhausted the graph routes to a graceful failure terminal that writes a failure artifact and terminates cleanly, and the synthesis node enumerates every branch with an explicit status naming failed branches and their error classes, so the run's terminal verdict is 'partial' rather than a success claim or an uncaught exception.

successCriteria.description: In a 3-branch fan-out where branch 2 throws, branches 1 and 3 results are persisted and the run continues; a re-run reuses the cached branch 1 and 3 results and their executor spies record zero additional invocations.

Only branch 2 is retried, successive retry timestamps match the configured jittered exponential policy within tolerance, and the branch 1 and branch 3 executors are invoked exactly once in total across the whole run.

A permanently failing node attempts exactly MAX_RETRIES times with a default of 3, then routes to the graceful-failure terminal, writes a failure artifact under .bober/failures/<runId>.json, and terminates cleanly with the test's own hard iteration ceiling never reached.

The runtime enforces each cycle's declared counterKey and maxIterations from the topology artifact, and a fixture graph whose loop would otherwise run forever exits by bound with a recorded bounded-exit span rather than by timeout.

The counter channel uses the idempotent maxNumber reducer, so replaying a superstep after a crash leaves the counter unchanged; a test replays a superstep and asserts the loop neither exhausts early nor gains an extra iteration.

The final synthesis output enumerates every branch with an explicit status and names each failed branch plus its error class, and the run's terminal verdict is 'partial' — not 'success' and not an uncaught exception.

branchStatus in state carries state, attempts and errorClass per branch key and merges through the lastWriteWinsByKey reducer over disjoint per-branch key domains, asserted by a concurrent-branch merge test.

A transient provider failure classified by the existing classifyTransient helper is retried while a non-transient failure is not, asserted by a table of error shapes covering HTTP 408, 429 and 5xx alongside a schema-validation failure.
npm run typecheck, npm run typecheck:tests, npm run build and npm run lint complete with zero errors and the full Vitest suite is green.

nonGoals: Do not retry a whole superstep or a whole fan-out batch when one branch fails; retry scope is the failed branch only.
Do not swallow a failure into a success verdict. A run with any exhausted branch terminates 'partial' or 'failed', never 'success'.
Do not write a new retry or backoff implementation; reuse withRetry and classifyTransient from src/orchestrator/workflow/retry.ts:61,103.
Do not implement the evaluator, critique or rework node bodies — sprint 12 builds those on top of this terminal and retry machinery.
Do not implement checkpoint persistence or interrupts; this sprint depends on sprint 7 only and must not duplicate sprint 8's work.

Do not let the graceful-failure terminal emit the pipeline-complete event directly; it produces a failure artifact and a verdict, and the single terminal side-effect owner from sprint 4 still emits the completion event.
stopConditions: The 3-branch partial-failure and cached-reuse assertions are both green.
The permanently failing node terminates by bound with a written failure artifact.
The counter replay test shows neither early exhaustion nor an extra iteration.
Meeting a criterion would require a non-idempotent counter reducer, which ADR-4 forbids.
value.definitionOfDone: A failing branch is retried in isolation on a jittered exponential schedule while its siblings' results are preserved and reused, every cyclic edge is bounded by the counter declared in the topology, exhausted retries route to a graceful terminal that writes a failure artifact, and synthesis reports per-branch status with a 'partial' verdict. The repository is shippable: typecheck, typecheck:tests, build and lint clean, full Vitest suite green, and no shipped execution path reaches this code.
assumptions: Scheduler.settle from sprint 7 is the mechanism by which a rejecting branch no longer rejects the whole batch; this sprint builds the policy on top of it rather than changing Scheduler again.
The branch result cache is the checkpoint's completedTaskKeys plus the committed branch outputs; it is not a second persistence store.

MAX_RETRIES defaults to 3 and is configurable; the topology's per-cycle maxIterations governs loop re-entry while MAX_RETRIES governs transient-failure retry, and the two are deliberately separate knobs.
outOfScope: Cross-run retry or resumption of a failed run from a previous invocation — sprint 8 owns resume.
Any latency or throughput assertion about retry scheduling; timestamps are asserted against the policy, not against wall-clock targets.
value.generatorNotes: Reuse workflow/retry.ts (withRetry at :61, classifyTransient at :103) and workflow/synthesizer.ts rather than writing new ones — both are green with near-zero live callers and this sprint gives them production callers. The retry timestamp assertion must be tolerant of jitter by construction: assert each interval falls inside the policy's min and max envelope rather than pinning exact values, and inject the clock so the test does not actually sleep. The graceful-failure terminal is a node in the topology (graceful_failure) whose body writes .bober/failures/<runId>.json and returns a terminal Command; it must not perform any other effect. Branch failure records carry branchKey, contractId, attempts and errorClass so synthesis can name them without reading the trace file.
value.evaluatorNotes: Verify the cached-reuse assertion counts executor invocations across BOTH runs, not just the second. Verify the retry test injects a clock and does not actually wait, and that it still asserts the interval envelope rather than merely counting attempts. Verify the terminal verdict for a partially failed run is 'partial' and that no code path can produce 'success' with a failed branch present. Verify the counter replay test replays a genuine superstep rather than calling the reducer twice in isolation. Confirm no new retry implementation was added alongside the existing one.

value.title: Engram context layer — phase digests with non-scalar diagnoses, clean-context handoff, and threshold-driven compression with an auditable transcript
value.description: Implement the persistent-archive-to-digest-to-fresh-context loop the source documents call Engram, mapped into the project-local .bober/ convention. On phase termination the terminating agent distills high-level insights, successful modelling choices, recommended next steps and specific failure diagnoses into one compact digest at .bober/handoff/<phase>-digest.md, validated by a schema that rejects a missing or empty section and requires at least one diagnosis carrying a hypothesis and its evidence — so a strategically better but temporarily regressing direction survives selection instead of being pruned by a bare score. The successor node launches with a fresh context that reads the digest first and imports no message id from the predecessor transcript. At superstep boundaries, message tokens above the configured fraction of the model's maximum input capacity trigger exactly one compression step producing a summary of active goals, completed tasks and the current workspace path, after which the baseline is that summary plus roughly the most recent tenth of the cap, with the full uncompressed transcript written to disk for auditability.

successCriteria.description: On phase termination a digest is written to .bober/handoff/<phase>-digest.md containing all four required sections, and a validator test fails the run when any section is missing or empty.

value.title: Node library part 1 — research subgraph with bounded reflexion, planner clarification loop, supervisor router and fail-closed schema gates
value.description: Implement the first half of the node library by wrapping the existing agent functions unmodified as node bodies. The Planner drafts, and when it needs clarification it surfaces questions, the run suspends through the sprint-8 interrupt mechanism, and supplying answers resumes the same planner node with those answers in its input — with no sprint contract materialised before the loop exits. Verification gates at every supervisor-to-subgraph boundary validate the traversing payload against the strict artifact schema and, on failure, do not merge the invalid payload into state, so bad intermediate data cannot propagate.

Given an ambiguous feature request the planner emits clarification questions and the run suspends; supplying answers resumes the same planner node with those answers present in its input, and a test asserts zero sprint contracts were materialised before the loop exited.

A gate fed a sprint contract missing successCriteria returns a typed failure, the downstream node's executor is never invoked, and the failure record contains the Zod issue path naming the missing field.

A structural test on the compiled research and plan subgraphs asserts maximum nesting depth is at most 2 and every subgraph exit edge targets the supervisor node.

value.title: Node library part 2 — sprint subgraph with curator mock-test gate, syntax gate, test anchors, correction loop, selective verification and gated documenter/commit
value.description: Implement the sprint subgraph as the topology declares it. The Curator explains each provided test's expected behaviour in natural language and generates 6 to 8 additional diverse mock tests covering boundary, empty, large and negative categories, enforced by a gate. Generated code passes a syntax and typecheck gate before reaching any downstream node, with compiler diagnostics attached verbatim to the rework payload on failure. The Evaluator maintains a registry of previously passed tests as anchors and rejects a self-healing edit that breaks an anchor even when it fixes the targeted test. On failure the correction payload carries raw stderr verbatim plus a brief critique and routes back to the generator, whose next prompt contains that payload, with the rework loop bounded by the topology's maxIterations. An evaluator that errors or returns malformed output routes to critique and never to success. Expensive suites run only when high-risk paths change or an intermediate quality score falls below threshold. A passing sprint reaches the documenter and produces a conventional commit behind the human-approval gate. Generated code and generated tests execute only through the sandbox runner.

successCriteria.description: Curator output contains one expectedBehavior string per provided or existing test; a test asserts the explanation count equals the input-test count and each explanation exceeds a configured minimum length.

The mock-test gate asserts the generated count is within [6,8] and that the set covers at least the boundary, empty, large and negative categories; a 5-case fixture and a fixture missing one category both fail the gate.
A gate fed code that does not typecheck blocks traversal, the evaluator node is never reached, and the compiler diagnostics are attached verbatim to the rework payload.

An integration test injects a failing implementation and asserts raw stderr appears verbatim in the correction payload, a non-empty critique accompanies it, the trace shows a route back to the generator node, and the second iteration's prompt contains that payload.
State carries testAnchors and an iteration that fixes the targeted test while breaking a previously passed anchor is flagged as a regression and rejected by the evaluator rather than accepted.
An evaluator that throws and an evaluator that returns malformed output both route to the critique node and never to the success node, with failClosed true recorded in the trace for each case.
A failing sprint re-enters the sprint subgraph at most maxIterations times with the critique present in each re-entry's input, then terminates via the graceful-failure path from sprint 9.

Three selective-verification cases hold: a docs-only diff skips the expensive suite node, a diff touching a declared high-risk path runs it, and a low-risk diff whose intermediate quality score is below threshold runs it anyway.

A passing sprint reaches the documenter node, a sprint doc file is written, and a conventional commit of the form bober(sprint-N): ... is produced only when the approval gate from sprint 8 has an approval record; a failing sprint produces no commit.

A generated test invoking a denied binary is rejected by the sandbox and recorded, and a non-terminating generated test is killed by the configured timeout rather than hanging the run; both route to correction and never to pass.

A fixture suite of model outputs containing multiline TypeScript with embedded double quotes parses at or above the pinned recovery rate in src/providers/structured.test.ts, and a control run of the same fixtures through a strict escape-sensitive path reproduces the failure mode the offloading discipline removes.

The sprint subgraph compiles independently from the committed artifact's subgraph declaration and executes end to end against stub providers, producing the same .bober/ artifact shapes the imperative sprint cycle produces.

value.title: Golden dataset, blocking CI structural-diff and regression gates, node-level documentation with drift enforcement, and the recorded engine migration disposition
value.description: Close the loop that makes the whole design pay: an artifact nobody gates on is an artifact nobody maintains. Commit a curated dataset of 20 to 50 golden cases with pinned provider responses and expected artifacts. Add one blocking pull-request CI job that runs the graph regression suite against that dataset behind a minimum pass-rate threshold, and in the same job runs pge dump --check, pge validate --mode full, pge docs --check, pge diff --require-version-bump against the base-branch artifact, and pge audit-state followed by git diff --exit-code — none with continue-on-error, so a stale artifact, an undocumented node or an unversioned structural change cannot merge regardless of review attention. Write docs/pge-graph.md covering every node, edge, gate and loop bound, kept in sync by the drift checker. Finally record the migration disposition in writing: PgeEngine remains opt-in with 'ts' as default, TsPipelineEngine is retained permanently as the oracle, the dormant src/orchestrator/workflow/ subtree's retention or conditional retirement is decided against the stated criteria, and the divergence of bober sprint and bober_sprint from the full sprint cycle is either resolved or formally documented as a deliberate escape hatch.

successCriteria.description: A test asserts the count of files under .bober/golden/ is within [20,50] and that each validates against a GoldenCase Zod schema containing input, pinned provider responses and expected artifacts.
Unit tests drive the regression runner at 79, 80 and 81 percent against a threshold of 80 and assert exit codes fail, fail and pass respectively.
A test parses .github/workflows/ci.yml and asserts a job exists that triggers on pull_request, invokes the graph regression runner, and does not set continue-on-error true.

The same workflow-parsing test asserts the blocking job also invokes pge dump --check, pge validate --mode full, pge docs --check, pge diff --require-version-bump and pge audit-state with git diff --exit-code, each without continue-on-error.

Both branches of the structural-diff rule are driven in unit tests: a non-empty topology diff without a graphVersion bump exits non-zero, and the same diff with a bump plus a changelog entry exits zero.

The diff gate uses structural mode so a base-branch artifact naming schema or prompt refs absent on head does not produce a spurious failure, asserted with a base fixture carrying an unknown promptRef.

docs/pge-graph.md exists and a doc-drift test asserts the set of node ids documented equals the set of node ids in the committed topology artifact; adding a node to a fixture artifact without documenting it fails the test.

docs/pge-graph.md documents, for every gate, what schema it validates and what it routes to on failure, and for every cyclic edge its counterKey, maxIterations and onExhausted target, asserted by a test that cross-checks those fields against the artifact rather than merely checking headings exist.
A test asserts config.pipeline.engine still defaults to 'ts' and that TsPipelineEngine is still constructible and still exercised by the conformance job, so the oracle is provably retained.

npm run typecheck, npm run typecheck:tests, npm run build and npm run lint complete with zero errors and the full Vitest suite is green.

Both branches of the version-bump rule are proven by unit tests rather than by trusting the workflow file.
The doc-drift test fails when a node is added without documentation.

The changelog entry required alongside a graphVersion bump is a section in docs/pge-graph.md rather than a separate file, so documentation and version history stay in one place the drift test already reads.
outOfScope: A quality benchmark measuring generation output against human judgement.
Flipping the default engine, which is a separate decision requiring sustained green conformance across real runs.
value.generatorNotes: Add the new job to the existing .github/workflows/ci.yml alongside build-and-test rather than creating a second workflow file, and make it need build-and-test so it runs on a built tree. The golden-case schema should reuse the existing conformance normalisation so expected artifacts are stored already stripped of volatile keys. For the diff gate, fetch the base artifact with git show <base>:.bober/topology/coding.json rather than a network call, so the gate works on forks and offline. The doc-drift checker already exists from sprint 3 — this sprint supplies the document and wires the check, it does not rewrite the checker. When recording the disposition, state the evidence: which workflow assertions are now green on the graph runtime, whether conformance is blocking, and what the pre-authorised end state is if conformance never converges.
value.evaluatorNotes: The central risk here is a gate that exists but does not bite. Verify each of the six checks by deliberately breaking its precondition in a test and asserting a non-zero exit: mutate the committed artifact, add an undocumented node to a fixture, change a fixture topology without bumping graphVersion, and stale the state audit. Verify the workflow-parsing test reads the real ci.yml and would fail if continue-on-error were added. Verify the golden dataset count assertion reads the directory rather than a hardcoded list. Verify no test file was deleted in this diff, and if a workflow module was deleted, verify the corresponding invariant has a passing counterpart on the graph runtime. Verify the documentation states the golden dataset's limitation explicitly.
